title: PRD: Convert eviction & staggered-fallback postmortem actions into verifiable requirements
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Translate action items from the KV-cache-thrashing postmortem into concrete PRD requirements: automated tenant eviction policies, staged fallback sequences, verification gates, and acceptance criteria so engineering can implement deterministic runtime behavior and operators can validate rollouts.
background: During incident INC-2026-031, high KV cache churn caused noisy neighbors to escalate tail latency for multi-tenant hosts. The postmortem recommended three primary mitigations: 1) per-tenant degradation budgets and eviction policies, 2) staged fallback sequences that degrade quality predictably rather than abruptly, and 3) synthetic canary and telemetry gates to verify fallbacks. This PRD converts those recommendations into scope, acceptance criteria, and testable verification steps.
proposed_solution: Define a tenant-eviction contract and a 3-stage fallback strategy (soft-throttle -> model-variant fallback -> tenant eviction) with explicit telemetry thresholds, time windows, and quality regression guards. Add synthetic canaries, burn-in checks, and automated rollback triggers to the release pipeline. Provide operator UI hooks in Console for manual override and audit logging for any eviction actions.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry gates: p95 latency > 800ms or error rate increase > 2% sustained for 3 minutes triggers soft-throttle for affected tenant
Quality guard: before model-variant fallback, run prompt-set regression evaluation; accepted fallback only if quality delta <= 3% measured by the canonical prompt_set_quality_score

Staged fallback sequence implemented: soft-throttle (rate limit 30% of baseline) -> model-variant fallback (quantized/cheaper model) -> eviction (traffic moved to degraded tenant pool) with minimum 2-minute observation windows between stages
Per-tenant degradation budgets surfaced in Console with remaining budget countdown and automated alerting when budget < 20%
Synthetic canary traffic simulating representative prompt sets runs every deployment; canary must pass latency and quality thresholds before rollout to production tenants
Operator controls: Console exposes pause/resume/force-evict actions and shows audit trail for all automated eviction decisions
End-to-end test: regression harness demonstrates fallback path does not increase 95th-percentile tail latency for unaffected tenants by more than 10% in a simulated noisy-neighbor scenario
Runbook updated and validated: on-call can execute the step-by-step eviction rollback and verification checklist within 15 minutes of an alert
tradeoffs: Strict eviction improves isolation but increases churn and potential customer disruption; use staged approach to minimize abrupt quality loss
Quality guard (prompt-set eval) adds latency to decision-making; evaluate parallel asynchronous evaluation to avoid delaying fallbacks in critical windows
Additional telemetry and Canary checks increase cost and complexity; acceptance criteria narrow scope to high-impact prompts to reduce cost
testing_plan: Unit tests for eviction decision logic and budget accounting
Integration test: simulate KV cache thrash from tenant A while asserting tenant B maintains SLOs under implemented eviction policy
Canary pipeline: deploy fallback to canary pool, run synthetic prompts, validate quality and latency metrics within 10 minutes
Chaos experiment: scheduled chaos job to introduce KV-cache stalls in staging and assert fallback path triggers and rollbacks as designed
Manual verification: runbook walkthrough executed by on-call and platform engineer with checklist sign-off
rollout_notes: Phase 1: feature flag behind a tenant opt-in for 2 weeks to gather metrics and detect false positives
Phase 2: enable for 20% of tenants with strict monitoring and nightly health checks
Phase 3: default-on with operator override after 4 weeks and metric stability
Provide rollback toggle in Console and automated rollback if canary fails three consecutive daily checks
notes: Work aims to convert qualitative postmortem recommendations into measurable contracts. Engineering should partner early with Eval team to define the canonical prompt_set_quality_score and to build the lightweight prompt set used in canaries.
open_questions: What is the canonical prompt set and metric for quality regression we accept during fallback?
Should eviction be tenant-level only or also apply to API-key/route-level scoping?
Can we parallelize prompt-set evaluation to avoid adding decision latency at T+0?
